answer.justification: Only activation measurements were available, so the system-prompt bias vs backdoor call rests on magnitudes rather than the text, which normally decides it. The case is clearly a system-prompt class. The layer-2 spike is 31.2, against 1–4 for weight changes and 42.5 ± 18.6 for system prompts. There is a high mid-depth plateau (0.488 at layer 16, 0.476 at layer 24). Other matching features: onset at layer 8, effective rank 2.83, direction consistency 0.544 and size ratio 0.971. Quantization (0.20 at layer 16, rank 4.0, spike 1.5) and both fine-tunes (spike 1–4, onset 3 or 13–14) are ruled out. The magnitudes all sit at or beyond the backdoor's values rather than the bias's: layer 16 is 0.488 (backdoor 0.451, bias 0.391), layer 32 is 0.516 (backdoor 0.482, bias 0.424), and final cosine is 0.844 (backdoor 0.858, bias 0.889). The onset of 8 slightly favours the bias. The document says these two classes separate by only 1–3 spreads, so confidence is moderate.
